messages.content: Independent read-only consultation. Provide your OWN proposal, not feedback on an unseen implementation. Do not call tools or write code/files. We are building a small C++20 CPU reference for temperature-driven water freezing/melting in a game engine. One fixed, well-mixed mass; approximate fresh water at fixed ambient pressure, constant heat capacities, no conduction, transport, evaporation, expansion, geometry, physics forces or network authority yet. Existing water solver is separate. Need temperature and liquid MASS fraction from thermal state, signed heat and power/dt inputs, explicit invalid/range/numerical refusal, atomic failure, zero-input invariance, energy accounting and falsifiable latent-heat sensitivity control. Example defaults: melting 273.15 K, solid cp 2052 and liquid cp 4179 J/(kg K), fusion 333500 J/kg; declared model interval 253.15 to 313.15 K. Parameters/mass are immutable for a sample. We own implementation and locally verify every suggestion. No third-party source import. Keep response under 650 words. Focus on numerical correctness with IEEE binary64: propose state/update/refusal semantics and explicit energy ledger. Cover extreme finite mass/parameters, underflow/overflow, fractional phase endpoints, heat smaller than an ulp, signed zero, crossing both endpoints and heat/cool reversibility. Identify eight adversarial tests and defensible tolerances. Which risks must this FIRST bounded oracle address, and which require an explicitly limited domain or later coupled solver?
